answer: I'd like to describe a day that made me happier than I had felt in a long time. A moment that filled me with genuine happiness was a spontaneous reunion with old friends I had not seen in years. We had all drifted apart after finishing our BBA, scattered by work and life, some in Dhaka, some in Chattogram and a couple abroad. Then, quite unexpectedly, one of them organised a get-together last winter, and almost everyone managed to come. I was so excited that I took the early morning bus from Sirajganj and arrived far too early. We met at a small restaurant near our old university campus in Dhaka. The moment we all saw each other again was absolutely [[heartwarming]]; it felt as though no time had passed at all. We spent hours [[reminiscing]], laughing about old memories and catching up on each other's lives. We even walked past our old classrooms and the tea stall where we used to spend far too much time. What made it so special was the [[effortless]], genuine warmth between us. In our busy adult lives, such [[carefree]] gatherings have become increasingly rare. I remember feeling completely content, surrounded by people who knew the real me. Honestly, that day reminded me how important old friendships are, and how easily we let them slip away. The whole reunion was thoroughly [[joyful]], and it left me determined to make more effort to stay in touch. We stayed so long that the restaurant staff eventually had to ask us, very politely, to leave. Since then, we have tried to meet at least once a year.

followUps.q: Do you find it hard to stay in touch with old friends?
followUps.answer: Sometimes, yes. Everyone is busy with work and family now. But a quick message or a phone call now and then keeps the connection alive, even if we can't meet often.

followUps.q: What else usually makes you happy?
followUps.answer: Simple things, mostly. A good dinner with my family, a cricket match on television, or a quiet walk by the river in the evening. I don't think happiness needs to be complicated.

note: Specified university friends and a reunion near their old campus in Dhaka; plain marks 'genuine' and 'rare' replaced by 'reminiscing', 'effortless', 'carefree'.
